_meta.note: Source file contains BDDS Mobile Accessibility page content

summary: Guidelines for creating mobile applications and websites that are inclusive and accessible to all people, regardless of ability or current usage context.
intent: Reduce cognitive effort across platforms through consistency.
Ensure visual information is perceivable under different abilities and contexts.
Make content understandable, navigable and screen-reader friendly.
Design interactions that are clear, reachable and usable with alternative inputs.

guidelines.title: Ensure a consistent experience across platforms
guidelines.rationale: A consistent experience requires less cognitive effort when switching between multiple platforms or products.
requirements: Use consistent components and navigation across multiple platforms and devices.
Use components that fit the app's context.
guidelines.ai: When evaluating or generating mobile UI, preserve interaction models, component behavior and navigation patterns across related products unless platform conventions or context require adaptation.

guidelines.title: Support customization
guidelines.rationale: Users have different visual, auditory, cognitive and motor needs, so a single solution often does not fit all.
requirements: Offer customization options such as languages, font sizes, contrast settings, notification settings and alternative input methods.
Support assistive technologies such as screen readers, large text and zoom features.
Retain accessibility settings across platforms.
guidelines.ai: A mobile experience should expose user-adjustable settings and avoid breaking when system-level accessibility settings are enabled.

guidelines.title: Test accessibility during development
requirements: Test mobile apps by changing font sizes and color spaces.
Activate VoiceOver on iOS and TalkBack on Android to verify that important information and interactive elements are perceivable.
guidelines.ai: Accessibility validation should happen during design and implementation, not only after release.

guidelines.title: Use high color contrast
guidelines.rationale: High color contrast makes important information visible to users with different levels of sight and under varying conditions, such as bright or low light.
requirements: Ensure sufficient contrast for important visual information.
Use dark mode carefully: dark mode may reduce eye strain for some users, but low-contrast dark themes can reduce readability or focus for others.
Provide customizable contrast options where relevant.

guidelines.title: Avoid highlighting crucial information solely with color
guidelines.rationale: People with impaired color perception may not perceive color-only distinctions.
requirements: Use additional symbols, labels, shapes or patterns when highlighting important information.
Use Android's Simulate color space tool to test color perception scenarios.

guidelines.title: Ensure that content is perceivable
guidelines.rationale: Users may rely on assistive technologies such as screen readers, zoom or large text.
requirements: Use accessibility labels for interactive elements such as form fields and buttons, especially icon-only elements.
Provide descriptive alt text and captions for images that convey meaning.
Do not integrate text into images; place text below images or use real text.
Provide feedback through multiple modalities, such as visual and haptic feedback.

guidelines.title: Ensure that content is simple, helpful and easy to navigate
guidelines.rationale: The small screen size on mobile devices makes clear information hierarchy and scannable content especially important.
requirements: Reduce content to the most essential information.
Start with the most important information and place it before the page scroll where possible.
Show details only when needed to reduce information density.
Group related information together and present it in a logical order.
Support both portrait and landscape orientation with a consistent layout.
Keep text clear, accurate and brief.
Avoid complicated sentences, technical terms and foreign words.

guidelines.title: Make sure users understand interactions
guidelines.rationale: Users should intuit or easily learn how to interact with the device so they can focus on their tasks.
requirements: Clearly distinguish interactive elements such as buttons and form fields.
Use BDDS components or native app components when appropriate because they are already optimized for usability.
Provide in-app training and instructions for gestures and device manipulation.

guidelines.title: Consider hand grip, size and physical limitations
guidelines.rationale: Users have varying hand sizes, phone-holding patterns and hand movement abilities.
requirements: Ensure that touch targets are appropriately spaced.
Use BDDS icon button spacing of 3x3 rem where applicable.
Provide easy and established touchscreen gestures and device manipulation options.
Provide alternatives for gestures and device manipulation when used for core functionality.

guidelines.title: Ensure user-friendly input
guidelines.rationale: Users may input information through voice, keyboard or switch input.
requirements: Make apps usable with alternative forms of input.
Support keyboard control for touchscreen devices where relevant.
Provide easy methods for data entry.

quality_checks: Are navigation and components consistent across related platforms?
Does the UI support system accessibility settings such as screen reader, zoom and large text?
Is important information visible with sufficient contrast?
Is crucial information not dependent on color alone?
Do all meaningful images have descriptive alt text or captions?
Are icon-only controls labeled for assistive technologies?
Is text real text rather than embedded in images?
Is content concise, logically grouped and prioritized for mobile screens?
Are alternatives provided for complex gestures or device manipulation?
Can users enter information through alternative input methods?
